summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with multiple myeloma, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, chronic hemolytic anemia, and dementia, was admitted after an unwitnessed fall resulting in a left intertrochanteric femur fracture. He underwent left hip hemiarthroplasty and was managed postoperatively for hospital-acquired pneumonia, likely aspiration-related, which presented with fevers and worsening lung infiltrates. He completed a 5-day course of broad-spectrum antibiotics followed by a 7-day course due to persistent fevers, after which he remained afebrile. He also experienced acute toxic-metabolic encephalopathy, which improved over time. His kidney function and hemoglobin stabilized, and he participated in physical therapy. He was discharged to extended care rehab with a plan for wound care, aspiration precautions, dialysis, and follow-up with orthopedics and oncology.
